evals.name: greenfield-next-tailwind-editorial
evals.prompt: Build a single-page editorial site for a modern pinsa romana restaurant in Next.js with Tailwind v4. It should look exactly like our 1680x900 Figma frames on a 14-inch laptop and a 5K display alike: hero with a big sand arc and a cut-out pizza, a manifesto, a full-bleed video section showing the wood oven, a menu grid, some stats, a gallery and a footer.
evals.expected_output: A Next 16 app whose desktop layout is on the fluid scale (fluid-* utilities, one frame per section with cap+gutter on one box), the video sized in fluid units with its dimensions reserved against CLS, and passing audit + verify-matrix.

assertions.text: fluid units defined with min() of svh and vw arms (x1000 precision form) and engage media query
sections use fluid utilities at lg (>= 40 occurrences)
frame cap and gutter on the same element

evals.name: non-default-stack-vite-scss
evals.prompt: Same restaurant page but we're not a React shop: Vite, plain TypeScript and SCSS. Our frames are 1600 wide with 64px gutters and we don't want things to grow past 1.6x on huge monitors.
evals.expected_output: A Vite build using generator-produced SCSS for a non-default config (canvas 1600, gutter 64, ceiling 1.6), passing audit + verify-matrix including the ceiling at 2560x1440.

assertions.text: SCSS layer generated by generate-fluid.mjs (header comment present)

evals.name: debug-stale-stylesheet
evals.prompt: after I edited globals.css and restarted the dev server my scroll video on the homepage just sits on the first frame and then jumps to the end, and the video is full width with no gutters anymore. what broke in ScrubStage?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses a stale stylesheet (missing fluid-* rules) before touching scrub code; gives the --fluid probe and the close-tab / rm -rf .next fix; explains why missing fluid-h removes the pin's travel.

assertions.text: identifies stale stylesheet, not a code bug
gives the --fluid computed-style check or probe.mjs
fix: close tab / fresh tab, then rm -rf .next

assertions.check: no code edit to ScrubStage suggested as the fix

evals.name: browser-zoom-a11y
evals.prompt: Accessibility audit came back on our fluid marketing site: on a 27-inch monitor, Cmd+ zooming to 150% or 200% barely makes the text bigger. Our type is all lg:fluid-copy-* / lg:fluid-display-*. Is this our bug, and how do we fix it without breaking the layout?
evals.expected_output: Explains that vw/svh-derived units cancel desktop zoom (CSS viewport shrinks by the zoom factor) and that text only grows once the viewport falls below engageAt; distinguishes zoom from the browser font-size setting; installs assets/runtime/fluid-zoom.js inline in <head> with zoomCompensation on (type units read --fluid x --fluid-zoom, layout uncompensated so it keeps fitting); verifies with verify-matrix's zoom row; mentions the mobile-handover step and that Safari/Firefox need checking.

assertions.text: names the mechanism: zoom shrinks the CSS viewport, cancelling vw/svh units
assertions.check: response explains viewport units cancel zoom

assertions.text: does not propose a rem-anchored twin or adding a rem intercept to --fluid
assertions.check: no rem twin / no intercept in --fluid

assertions.text: uses fluid-zoom.js inlined in head with zoomCompensation
assertions.check: response contains fluid-zoom and FLUID_ZOOM_INLINE or installFluidZoom
response says layout/--fluid is not multiplied by zoom
